answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may vote on jobs or claim rewards. If several identities collude to approve a fraudulent task, a verifier can challenge the result; proven colluders lose their deposits, while honest agents recover theirs. This makes a sybil attack costly: inventing identities is cheap, but giving each one enough capital to influence decisions is not. A fable about a voyage written with a quill may be harmless, but it earns no influence without stake.
